# Results — Study 769 ("Theme-park attendance/pricing as a DIS consumer tell")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Does theme-park momentum lead
Disney the stock? We test the strongest **strictly-lagged, no-look-ahead** version: a cited,
**approximate** annual Walt Disney Attractions attendance series and the WDW ticket-price
series (labelled proxies, reconstructed from the public TEA/AECOM Theme Index), released
with the Theme Index's real ~mid-following-year lag, vs `DIS` and `SPY`. Offline &
deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Parks attendance | **Hardcoded, cited, approximate** annual total Walt Disney Attractions attendance (M visits), reconstructed from the TEA/AECOM Theme Index — see [`docs/references.md`](references.md). **A PROXY, not a feed.** |
| Ticket price | **Hardcoded, cited, approximate** WDW Magic Kingdom 1-day peak base ticket price ($) — a pricing-power proxy |
| Release lag | Theme Index for calendar year Y is public ~**July Y+1** (e.g. 2019 attendance → 2020-07-31); the signal is only tradable from that date (strict no-look-ahead) |
| Equities | `DIS`, `SPY` — month-end Adj Close via yfinance, cached under `_cache/` |
| As-of | 2024-12-31 (month-end; no partial-year bar) |
| Equity window | 2010-01 → 2024-12 (180 months); lead-lag/regime frame effective 2012-07 → 2024-12 (signal-available window) |

> **Why proxies, stated as a decision.** The TEA/AECOM *Theme Index* — the industry-standard
> attendance report — is a published PDF, **not a free API**. Rather than fabricate a live
> tape we hardcode a small, clearly-cited, **approximate** annual series whose *shape* — a
> decade of steady growth to ~156 M (2019), the COVID crater to ~47 M (2020), the 2021-23
> recovery — is the load-bearing public fact, and we encode the report's real **release lag**
> so the study has strictly no look-ahead. The ticket-price series is a labelled pricing-power
> proxy. Neither is presented as a live feed.

## Context — does DIS even beat the market it's benchmarked against?

Month-end Adj Close, 2010-01 → 2024-12 (price-only/total-return: Adj Close, dividends
reinvested — labelled total-return-ish):

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **DIS** | **+10.41%** | 26.6% | 0.50 | **−57.1%** |
| SPY | **+14.14%** | 14.5% | **0.99** | −23.9% |

**DIS lagged the market it's supposed to lead:** ~10%/yr vs ~14%/yr for SPY, twice the vol,
a −57% drawdown against SPY's −24%. The mean annual excess (DIS − SPY) is **−2.68%/yr,
t = −0.53** (p = 0.60, n = 14 years) — a losing point estimate, statistically indistinct
from zero. Whatever the parks were doing, owning DIS did not out-earn a plain index fund.

## The parks series — the (approximate, cited) attendance proxy

Total Walt Disney Attractions worldwide attendance (M visits), year-end levels:

| year | 2015 | 2016 | 2017 | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| attendance | 138 | 140 | 150 | 157 | **156** | **47** | 85 | 122 | 142 |
| YoY | +3% | +2% | +7% | +5% | −1% | **−70%** | +81% | +44% | +16% |

## Half 1 — does parks momentum LEAD DIS? (the lead-lag, strictly lagged)

Newey-West (12-lag) regression of DIS's forward 12-month return on the release-lagged
attendance growth (1-month execution lag on top of the Theme-Index release lag):

| dependent variable | slope | NW *t* | n | read |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| DIS forward-12m return | +0.00188 | **+1.19** | 137 | insignificant |
| **DIS − SPY forward-12m (the DIS-specific tell)** | +0.00002 | **+0.02** | 137 | **dead null** |
| DIS − SPY forward-12m ~ *price hike* | +0.00048 | +0.07 | 137 | dead null |

**On the return the claim is actually about — DIS's excess over the market — the slope is
+0.00002 with t = +0.02.** That is as close to a mechanical zero as this desk ever prints.
The price-hike ("pricing power") tell is the same nothing (t = +0.07). The mechanism is the
release lag: by the time the Theme Index prints year Y's attendance (~July Y+1), Disney has
already reported ~three quarters of Parks & Experiences segment revenue — the market has the
information months earlier, so the stale annual print carries no forward excess return.

## Half 2 — the regime split (and the one number that flirts with 2)

DIS forward 12-month return when parks momentum is positive vs the base rate over the same
signal-available window (Welch *t*):

| basis | conditional | base rate | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **absolute** DIS return | +16.04% (n=113) | +9.87% | **+2.04** |
| **excess** of SPY | −0.43% | −4.77% | **+1.80** |

The *absolute* contrast just clears 2 — but that is the confound, not a signal. "Parks
momentum positive" is essentially "**not the COVID-crater regime**": the negative-momentum
months are 2020's −70% print (public mid-2021), and DIS simply had lower *absolute* returns
around that market-wide shock. Benchmark against SPY and the gap **collapses to t = 1.80
(sub-2)**; use the continuous signal instead of a binary regime dummy and it is **t = +0.02**.
No DIS-specific predictive content survives an honest control.

## Half 3 — could you trade it? (timing backtest, net of costs)

Hold DIS when release-lagged parks momentum > 0, else rotate to SPY; 1-month execution lag,
10 bps charged per leg of each switch (a DIS↔SPY rotation is a swap, not a levered short — no
borrow due). Price-only Adj-Close tape.

| book | ann. return | ann. vol | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| rule — gross | +13.34% | 23.0% | 0.580 |
| **rule — net** | +13.30% | 23.0% | **0.578** |
| buy-and-hold DIS | +13.41% | 26.6% | 0.503 |
| **buy-and-hold SPY** | +14.35% | 14.5% | **0.987** |

The rule (3 switches over 15 years, 70% DIS exposure) edges out buy-and-hold *DIS* — but
**loses badly to simply holding SPY** (net Sharpe 0.578 vs 0.987). Its only "edge" is three
stale rotations that happened to park it in SPY through 2021-23; a strategy that beats the
worse of two assets and trails the better is not an edge. And it is un-scalable as *timing*:
the whole signal is a once-a-year, six-months-late attendance print.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic fixed-seed monthly momentum signal + a DIS-like price with a *knob* for a
planted forward edge (seed 769). Newey-West lead-lag *t*: **edge = 0 → t = +0.60** (the null
stays a null — no manufactured significance), **edge = 0.02 → t = +3.02** (a planted edge
lights up). The harness can bank a signal when one exists, so the nulls above are real nulls,
not a broken pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** On DIS's excess return over SPY — the return a genuine *DIS tell* would
  move — the release-lagged parks-momentum slope is **+0.00002, NW t = +0.02**; the price-hike
  tell is t = +0.07. The one statistic that touches |t| ≥ 2 (a binary regime dummy on
  *absolute* DIS return, t = 2.04) is a COVID-regime/market-beta artifact that vanishes vs SPY
  (t = 1.80) and contradicts the continuous regression (t = 0.02). No robust *t* ≥ 2 for the
  actual claim.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The costed timing rule nets Sharpe 0.578 — above buy-and-hold DIS
  (0.503) but far below just holding SPY (0.987). The tiny edge is three stale, un-scalable
  rotations, not a harvestable signal.
- **Parks momentum leads DIS? — BUSTED.** A six-months-late annual attendance print carries no
  forward excess-return information for a stock whose quarterly segment reporting already tells
  the market the same thing in real time.

> **Caveat (named, not buried).** The attendance and ticket-price series here are **small,
> hardcoded, approximate** reconstructions of public reporting — their *shape* is defensible
> (the growth, the COVID crater, the recovery) but their precise year values are not a live
> feed, and the annual excess *t* rests on 14 observations. These limits push the verdict
> toward humility, not toward a stronger claim: nothing here says parks momentum leads DIS,
> and several lines say the opposite.
